blueprint_topic: Management of Care — transplant evaluation and longitudinal care coordination
stem: A client undergoing kidney-transplant evaluation has multiple tests, specialist visits, and follow-up requirements and asks who helps organize this process. Which response by the RN is most accurate?

options.A: The clinical transplant coordinator arranges evaluation, treatment, and follow-up care and works with the transplant team throughout the process.
options.B: The clinical transplant coordinator mainly manages financial authorization, while other team members separately arrange clinical testing and follow-up.
options.C: The clinical transplant coordinator reviews completed testing and makes the transplant program's final listing decision before arranging follow-up.
options.D: The clinical transplant coordinator coordinates the evaluation, but the role generally ends when the transplant program accepts the client for listing.

rationale: A is correct. Current HRSA/OPTN patient guidance states that clinical transplant coordinators are nurses or other health professionals who arrange a transplant patient's evaluation, treatment, and follow-up care. HRSA's kidney-transplant evaluation guidance separately states that a transplant program must evaluate and accept a person before listing and that each transplant program makes its own decision about candidate acceptance. HRSA also distinguishes financial coordinators from clinical transplant coordinators and describes ongoing testing and follow-up while listed and after transplant. B is incorrect because financial matters are a distinct financial-coordinator function and the clinical transplant coordinator has an explicit clinical care-coordination role. C is incorrect because candidate acceptance/listing is a transplant-program decision rather than an independent decision of one coordinator. D is incorrect because the coordinator's role includes follow-up care and is not limited to the prelisting evaluation phase.
educational_objective: Recognize the clinical transplant coordinator as a longitudinal care-coordination resource who arranges evaluation, treatment, and follow-up while the transplant program/team retains responsibility for candidate acceptance and listing decisions.
source_organization: Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) / Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN)
source_document_title: The Transplant Team; Frequently Asked Questions About Kidney Transplant Evaluation and Listing; Transplant Process
source_version_date: Current HRSA/OPTN patient guidance rechecked 2026-08-20; pages were current in the HRSA OPTN patient-resource set at time of audit
source_locator: HRSA/OPTN — The Transplant Team: clinical transplant coordinators are nurses or other health professionals who arrange the patient's evaluation, treatment, and follow-up care; financial coordinators handle financial matters and hospital billing. HRSA — Frequently Asked Questions About Kidney Transplant Evaluation and Listing, 'What do I need to do to be considered for a transplant?': a transplant program must evaluate and accept the person before listing, and each transplant program makes its own candidate-acceptance decision; evaluation includes multiple medical and psychosocial/support assessments with ongoing testing while listed. HRSA — Transplant Process, Patient notification: the transplant hospital/program makes the listing decision and must notify the patient of listing or nonlisting outcomes.
source_claim_supported: Current HRSA/OPTN guidance directly supports the clinical transplant coordinator's role in arranging evaluation, treatment, and follow-up and distinguishes this coordination role from transplant-program listing decisions and financial-coordinator duties.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care — Collaboration with Multidisciplinary Team, Referrals, Case Management, and Continuity of Care: identify and collaborate with appropriate team members, coordinate complex services/referrals, communicate significant information, act as liaison/coordinator, and support continuity and follow-up across settings and treatment phases.
pdf_visual_verification: The HRSA/OPTN evidence relied upon for this item is current HTML; no HRSA PDF is relied upon. Relevant NCSBN 2026 Management of Care collaboration/case-management content had been visually verified earlier in this audit session.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'kidney transplant clinical coordinator evaluation treatment follow-up listing transplant team' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the transplant-coordination construct but removed the 'only operating room' and financial-only absolute distractors and balanced the key. The revised alternatives test realistic role confusion among clinical coordination, financial coordination, transplant-program listing authority, and the duration of coordinator involvement.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly matches HRSA's definition of the clinical transplant coordinator and preserves team-based longitudinal coordination.
option_audit.B: Plausible role-confusion error; incorrect because financial authorization/billing is a distinct financial-coordinator function and clinical coordinators arrange clinical care.
option_audit.C: Plausible authority-overreach error; incorrect because the transplant program/team, not a coordinator acting independently, determines candidate acceptance/listing.
option_audit.D: Plausible phase-limitation error; incorrect because clinical transplant coordination includes follow-up care and continues beyond initial evaluation/listing.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes.
cueing_audit.answer_length: All four alternatives contain comparable role/process detail; the key is not uniquely signaled by length.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel descriptions of the clinical transplant coordinator's role.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after current HRSA/OPTN source-based audit and targeted repository search.
